name: Capixyl
lead: Capixyl is a trademarked cosmetic hair-care active from Lucas Meyer Cosmetics, now part of Clariant, used in leave-on and rinse-off hair serums and shampoos aimed at thinning hair and sparse lashes. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, describes it as a combination of the peptide acetyl tetrapeptide-3 with red clover (Trifolium pratense) flower extract standardised for the isoflavone biochanin A.[1] People use products containing it as a topical option to hold on to density and look for fuller, thicker-looking hair.

The supplier says the complex works on several fronts: anchoring follicles in the scalp, moderating DHT activity, calming inflammation and supporting scalp balance.[1] Grokipedia gives typical use concentrations of 1.5 to 5 percent.[1] Independent human data on Capixyl alone are limited; much of the quoted efficacy comes from supplier material or from tests of combinations with other actives.[1][2]

A 2025 review of hyped topical hair-growth actives lists Capixyl alongside Redensyl, Procapil, Baicapil and AnaGain, finding that these ingredients have mostly been studied in combined formulations, with promising results but small samples, conflicts of interest and limited comparison with standard therapies.[2]

chain: Serum with acetyl tetrapeptide-3 and red clover extract applied to scalp
Claimed follicle anchoring, lower DHT activity and calmer scalp
angle.text: Capixyl is used in topical hair serums by people who want thicker-looking hair or a non-drug add-on to other hair-loss routines. The supplier's pitch is that it keeps follicles anchored and reduces DHT-driven thinning.

infobox: Cosmetic active ingredient (peptide plus plant extract)
Acetyl tetrapeptide-3, red clover extract (biochanin A)

paras: Per Grokipedia, acetyl tetrapeptide-3 is a short biomimetic signal peptide that is said to raise collagen III and laminin in fibroblasts, supporting the anchoring of follicles in the scalp, while the red clover extract, rich in biochanin A, is credited with inhibiting 5-alpha reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone to DHT.[1] The source cites cell assays in which biochanin A at 100 micromolar inhibited type I and type II isoforms by about 64 and 93 percent, and notes that this is not evidence of an effect on scalp DHT in users.[1]

Grokipedia also credits the red clover component with anti-inflammatory properties and the complex with supporting scalp microbiota balance.[1] Some web sources confuse Capixyl with Procapil, which contains biotinoyl tripeptide-1; they are separate products from different suppliers.[1]

Capixyl was developed by Lucas Meyer Cosmetics. Grokipedia reports a trademark application filed in March 2014 and registered in March 2015, and Clariant's completion of its acquisition of Lucas Meyer Cosmetics in April 2024.[1]

No independent published trial of Capixyl on its own was found. A 2025 review in the International Journal of Trichology examined 24 articles and technical files on Redensyl, Procapil, Capixyl, Baicapil, AnaGain and several botanical ingredients, and reported that they were mostly studied as combined formulations in randomised trials or prospective cohorts, with limited sample sizes, a lack of comparison with standard therapies and conflicts of interest; the authors suggest they may suit add-on or alternative use.[2]

Grokipedia mentions an open-label comparison with 5 percent minoxidil of a combination of Redensyl, Capixyl and Procapil, in which more combination users were reported as improved, and notes that sample size and blinding details are absent and that the test did not isolate Capixyl.[1]

Grokipedia says supplier assessments report no local adverse reactions, without naming a specific study. It describes Capixyl as a cosmetic ingredient, so products containing it are sold as cosmetics rather than approved hair-loss drugs.[1]

card.summary: A peptide and red clover blend in hair serums; claims rest mostly on supplier data and combination tests.
card.aka: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3 and red clover complex
card.note: No independent single-ingredient human trial found.

quick.overview:
Capixyl is a cosmetic ingredient combining a peptide with red clover extract, sold for use in anti-hair-loss serums.

The supplier cites reduced shedding, but the available sources give few independent human data.
quick.mechanism: Claimed to improve follicle anchoring via collagen and laminin, and to inhibit 5-alpha reductase through biochanin A; lab-level support cited by Grokipedia is at high concentrations.
quick.risks: No specific adverse effects are documented in the sources; it is regulated as a cosmetic and is not an approved treatment for hair loss.
